method: Synthesis of (1) audit_research.json MTFS data + (2) savings_recommendations.json strategic themes + (3) cross-sector benchmarks library (burnley-council/data/shared/savings_benchmarks_library.json) gated by council tier + PFI/ALMO/LATCo/audit-opinion flags. Each additional opportunity is verified as NOT in the council's existing programme.

context.lgr_status: confirmed - abolition of Thurrock Council from April 2028

existing_programme.title: Remediate disclaimed audit opinion (BDO LLP, year ended 2020-03-31)
existing_programme.rationale: External auditor issued a DISCLAIMED opinion on financial statements. Concerns: Multi-year audit backlog spanning 2020/21 through 2023/24; council pushing BDO to complete 2020/21 with a disclaimed opinion (3-year delay); 2024/25 draft Statement of Accounts were not available for public inspection by the statutory deadline of 30 June 2025 - audit process still in progress; Section 114 notice issued 19 December 2022 reporting an in-year funding gap of £470m and structural deficit in 2023/24 of £184m. Direct savings: PSAA scale fee normalisation (current scale fee £250K + disclaimer surcharge). Indirect: lifting MHCLG governance flag reduces borrowing-cost premium (typically 5-15bp on new external debt) + opens £M of grant programmes that require unmodified opinions. Foundation requirement before ANY other transformation saving is credible to auditor or DLUHC.

existing_programme.title: Agency / locum staff demand reduction (£39M concentrated)
existing_programme.rationale: £39M of agency-staff spend across 1 master vendors. Top: MATRIX SCM LTD (£39M). Standard transformation: cap agency premium at 20% above substantive rate, workforce-plan permanent conversion (6-9 month payback), regional bank pool, open-book master-vendor margins. CIPFA experience: 8-15% reduction in 12-18 months.

existing_programme.title: Energy procurement via CCS / LASER / NEPO frameworks (£8M baseline)
existing_programme.rationale: £8M utility spend across 2 suppliers. Top: EDF ENERGY (£7M), TOTALENERGIES (£1M). Crown Commercial RM6306 + LASER / NEPO consortium flex purchase typically saves 4-8% vs direct supplier contracts on a 3-yr horizon. Plus solar PV self-generation on council estate (7-9 yr payback) + DESNZ Public Sector Decarbonisation Scheme grants up to 100% capex on heat pump conversion.

existing_programme.title: Treasury management + borrowing cost optimisation (CFR proxy £161M)
existing_programme.rationale: Annual revenue £202M implies indicative CFR c. £161M. Standard levers: internal borrowing from earmarked reserves, PWLB Certainty Rate trade, MMF counterparty restructuring, LGPS Property Investment Pool inclusion. 10-30bp saving on external debt typical from a fresh review.

existing_programme.title: LGPS employer contribution opportunity (2025 triennial valuation cycle)
existing_programme.rationale: Indicative pay bill £81M × c. 22% employer contribution rate = £18M annual employer contribution. Most LGPS funds materially over-funded post-2022 (returns 2022-25 averaged 7-10% pa vs 3-4% discount-rate assumption). 2025 triennial valuation typically yields 2-4pp employer-rate reduction over 2026-2029. Confirm with administering authority + actuary.

existing_programme.title: Fees, charges + traded-services income optimisation (£20M base)
existing_programme.rationale: Indicative fees & charges + traded-services income c. 10% of revenue = £20M. Standard levers: annual CPI uplift discipline, full-cost-recovery audit on discretionary services (parking, planning, licensing, sports, adult learning, property hire), commercial pricing on traded services. LGA experience: 5-15% income uplift sustainable over 2-3 years.

existing_programme.title: Insurance retention + premium review (£0.2M premium estimate)
existing_programme.rationale: Indicative insurance premium £0.2M (10bp of revenue). Standard 3-5 yr renewal cycle. Levers: tender via IPG / RM Partners (10-25% premium reduction typical), retention review (increase excess + build risk-fund reserve). London-borough cohort average 12% premium reduction at last tender.

existing_programme.title: Contracts Finder portfolio review (159 notices; 2 contracts at £10M+ ceiling)
existing_programme.rationale: Contracts Finder data: 159 notices (83 awarded, £107M aggregate ADVERTISED CEILING value, 0% SME). IMPORTANT: advertised contract value is a CEILING set to avoid retender risk under PCR 2015 Reg.72 / Procurement Act 2023 s.31 — actual spend through the awardee is typically 30-70% of ceiling, with some off-contract ledger spend permitted within the 50%/50% modification limits. 2 contracts at £10M+ ceiling totalling £52M (ceiling, NOT spend) — top 3: Temporary Agency Worker Resources (ceiling £42M); Decarbonisation Retrofit (ceiling £10M). Matched against ledger: ICT Hardware — ceiling £1.7M, actual ledger spend with awardee £0.2M; Oracle Support — ceiling £0.3M, actual ledger spend with awardee £0.3M; Traffic Enforcement Cameras — ceiling £0.2M, actual ledger spend with awardee £0.5M. Aggregate identified actual spend £6624M. SME-awarded share 0% is below the Procurement Reform 2023 / PPN 03/24 ambition (33% SME share by value). Standard procurement-data savings levers (% of ACTUAL ledger spend, not ceiling): (a) modification-history scrutiny under PCR 2015 Reg.72, (b) Procurement Act 2023 s.31 contract change notice review, (c) re-tender benchmark vs CCS framework rates on next renewal. 2-8% on actual spend through major contracts is a defensible upper bound.

existing_programme.title: Refund / credit-note management + contract dispute resolution (£75M, 1,731 rows)
existing_programme.rationale: 1,731 negative-amount rows totalling £75M — refunds, credit notes, contract reversals. Volume signals correct ledger capture, but proactive levers exist: (a) contract management review on top recurring refund counterparties, (b) duplicate-payment pre-detection, (c) energy-bill credit-management automation. Typical 5-10% reduction in refund volume + faster reconciliation = 10-30bp net cash improvement.

existing_programme.title: Audit + recover £140M in flagged duplicate-payment patterns
existing_programme.rationale: DOGE forensic flagged £140M across 1,689 groups of likely duplicates. Industry recovery norm 5-15% via duplicate-detection software (AP Forensics, FISCAL, Oracle Concur). Lloyds Bank Commercial Card analysis typical for spot-check sample of 100 highest-confidence matches.

additional_opportunities.name: HNSG Local SEND Reform Plan submission — 90% DSG write-off
additional_opportunities.lever_description: Government announced 9 Feb 2026 (alongside final 2026/27 LGFS) that 90% of every English council's accumulated DSG deficit at 31 March 2026 will be written off via a new Section 31 grant — the High Needs Stability Grant (HNSG), worth ~£5.6Bn nationally. Conditional on the council submitting an approved Local SEND Reform Plan to DfE by **19 June 2026**; grants paid Autumn 2026. Safety Valve programme closed 1 April 2026 (folded into HNSG). Statutory override extended to 31 March 2028; gov committed to absorb ALL DSG deficits from 1 April 2028. New 2026/27 + 2027/28 deficits NOT yet covered — linked to demonstrable delivery on approved reform plan (OBR forecast: £8.6Bn additional deficits over those two years).
additional_opportunities.council_specific_rationale: Residual 10% management — plan submission unlocks 90% auto write-off

case_studies.horizon: Autumn 2026 grant; conditional on 19 June 2026 plan submission
case_studies.note: £67.7M deficit → ~£60.9M write-off, ~£6.8M residual. Not previously a Safety Valve participant.
£17M → ~£15.3M write-off, ~£1.7M residual. 2026/27-2028/29 budget approved on HNSG assumption.
Active Safety Valve participant 2022-23 cohort. £17.8M → ~£14.4M HNSG write-off, ~£1.6M residual after SV local contributions count toward 10%.
~£180M at 31 Mar 2026 → ~£162M write-off, ~£18M residual. Not Safety Valve. Reform UK took control 8 May 2026 — plan submission is most material early decision.
